t: Discuss the information obtained from Broga with saboteur Larisa Dymkina.

Fiery Father talk to ours... Order to whack worms-on-faces... Worms-on-faces be enemy. Become friend. Now again enemy. Our fights!
Worms-on-faces fights cowardly! They sits under the ground. Operates golem! Golem go, ours fight. Fight strong! But ours not give in. Ours breaks golem. Search worms-on-faces. Search under the grounds! When they goes out, pull them out and whack! And then yum! That's it. Worms-on-faces few. Golem many! But golem can't be yum. Ours try... Tooth crack, crack. Now our tooth hurt...
Fiery Father say if all worms-on-faces dies, only ours stay. Ours go to City on Bones. Ours seek strange thing! Strange thing save ours. World crack! Boom! Ours stay safe. Ours go far away and stay safe. Other burns. Fiery Father say so!

So that's it... Turns out their Fiery Father knew everything beforehand. And the betrayal was carefully planned. And the only reason the Fiery Father has entered into an alliance with the Master was to gain access... To what? It'd be great if we could find out more about that.

Hey, soldier! Why are you hanging around here? Got nothing to do?
I'll find a task for you, no problem! We're few in number, so every blade is a blessing.
Recently the draconids have increased their raids on the Outpost. We've been holding our ground so far, but each attack takes a toll and I don't know how long we can go on. So, please do me a favor and give the draconids hell! I want them to forget the way to this place!
A draconid is just a big lizard. I wonder why they don't shed their tails when in danger?

Aha! Take that, you scaly scum! Leave us alone!
Thank you so much, pal! I don't know what we'd do without you.
Participate in killing the wormface dominator and return to Agatha Grekhova at the Outpost.

We're sick and tired of those golems! Not that they pose a real threat... But they're getting more organized by the day!
I think that whichever wormface is operating the golems have picked our camp as a training ground. That doesn't make me happy at all, and that's putting it lightly.
Will you help us? The scum operating the golems ought to have his facial tentacles tied around his ass! I think he's hiding somewhere north of the Outpost. But to lure him out from under ground where those cowards usually hide, you'll need a thunderstone. Toss it inside the hiding place and the tentacle-faced bastard will bolt out at once!
And be sure to take some friends with you! I have a feeling that wormface will prove tougher than others.

It's a pity golems can't be re-subdued to our will. They would make perfect fighters, what with their great strength and stamina, no need for food, never falling asleep at the post, never getting hammered at some tavern...
The golem commander is no more? Excellent! Thank you so much!
Participate in killing Grosh, the draconid leader, and return to Agatha Grekhova at the Outpost.

Gosh, am I angry! This draconid named Grosh is apparently quite the joker. What a bastard!
Every night he gets on top of a hill and starts flashing me all kinds of indecent gestures! And more than just gestures... I'm going to... I'll... I'd strangle the bastard with my bare hands for such insinuations!
Only I can't leave the camp. And that bastard is obviously mocking me on purpose. Once my fighters and I set out to beat his skull in, but apparently there's a whole squad of them behind the hill... A real trickster, that one!
How would you like to defend a maiden's honor? Find Grosh and smash his mug in so he can't even walk. But beware - he's a tough cookie! You shouldn't go after him by yourself. Big bastards like him should be taken on with a group, just in case.
After such boorish behavior, I wouldn't give a dented penny to save Grosh's life!

That's it! Thank you, friend!
Now, those friggin' lizards will think twice before showing such vulgar things to an honest girl!

Goodness gracious... I couldn't dream that you'd handle war machines that were designed to kill with such ease.
 This clearly shows that mind is superior to technology!
You know, looking at an attacking golem you'd never think all it is, is clay, sand, iron and some magic.
Get a wormface's brain, use the transmitter to summon Sarbaz Gurguf, give him the brain and receive further instructions.

Wait, don't distract me. I'm thinking... Thinking... Thinking... Damn it, you distracted me!
What do you want? Just saying hi? What impudence! I was one step away from a spectacular discovery. Now I've lost my train of thought because of you!
All right, listen, now that I'm distracted, you might as well make yourself useful.
I'm researching psionic capabilities of those you call "wormfaces." Their true name is far more complicated, you wouldn't even be able to pronounce half of it.
Now, do you know that wormfaces can have tremendous influence on your mind? That's right. I want to understand where they get that power and how it is generated...
I need their brain! Fresh and intact. I sense that it conceals lots of mysteries.
What's in it for you? How about fame and respect of the entire scientific community?!
However, I need an absolutely fresh brain! While you carry it around in your backpack, all the neural connections will be lost. This is why I'm giving you the transmitter. When you get the brain, press the big red button. Then, guided by the signal, I'll be able to get to you under cover of invisibility. I hope the wormfaces won't spot me... I'd do anything for the sake of science!
Alpha chromosome, beta chromosome, genetic changes, mutation... No, that's not what I need!

Hrm. Was the patient struck on the head with a heavy object? Was the specimen extracted carefully and without injury? Listen, I know your idea of "anesthesia": smack the patient's head with a club, and there you go.
Get a Keeper's brain, use the transmitter to summon Sarbaz Gurguf, give him the brain and receive further instructions.

Interesting... Wait a minute, let me think.
If they have unstable connections, that means... What about the cause for the development of stable psionic heredity? No, no, that's not it at all!
Listen. The brains I have are no good. I can't understand what the secret is.
You'll have to continue searching and get me new materials to study. I reckon a Keeper's brain would be useful. I trust you have a thunderstone with you? Without it you won't have a chance going up against a Keeper.
When you're done, use the transmitter and hand over the research material to me.
I wonder if the Keepers have developed naturally or were bred Perhaps they hold the same status as the termite queen?

Is this a brain? It is. One unit. Looks like a normal brain.
Strange... It's not quite normal! Look, there's a strange spot here near the hypothalamus...
Wait, you mean that's dirt from your grimy hands?! Oh, astral demons take me! You don't handle valuable research materials in this fashion!
Get a Samum's brain, use the transmitter to summon Sarbaz Gurguf, give him the brain and receive further instructions.

So, the first sample of the wormface's cerebrum is useless and the second one is ruined. What can we do? Here's what we'll do.
I heard from Kirill Pryatkin that he'd met a unique wormface in the depths of the cave. Kirill is a sly fellow and shifty as a rat, and even he barely managed to survive.
Wouldn't it be great to acquire the cerebrum of this monster? Just think how it would aid our research! But don't go charging into battle just yet or he will turn your brains to jelly before you can say your prayers. My scientific experience suggests that this wormface is a serious enemy. You had better gather all of your friends before attempting to sever the wormface from his cerebrum.
But don't delay either, for I'm all feverish with anticipation of the mysteries it may reveal! We're talking a guaranteed new scientific degree! Use the transmitter as soon as you are done. And remember that every minute of my time is precious.
Did you manage to get the brain I need? Science can't wait!

Wow! That is something... This is the first time I see a brain so complicated and highly developed!
I bet that the creature this brain belonged to used much more than just 10 percent of it... I could have been 100, maybe even 120! I sincerely regret its death, but science demands sacrifice!
OK, I'm heading back to my lab to start studying it.
And you ought to get a reward for your contribution to science. Take your pick!
Meet Yaver Tul at the excavations near the Hissing Canyon.

Wait up! I was requested to give you a message.
Yaver Tul, our best technician, asked someone resembling a battle-hardened hero to meet her in the excavations area. She needs a tight-lipped and quick-witted assistant who could hold their own. And you fit the bill just right!
Yaver Tul is a genius when it comes to war mechanisms. Her hands are made of gold! Well, they look ordinary prosthetics on the outside, but the internal circuits are golden! Trust me, that makes a big difference.
If you prove useful to her, Yaver Tul will reward you generously. So go on, get to the excavations.

Ah, so you're the "greatest hero of the past, present and future," as my colleague described you? Odd, you don't look too formidable at all.
But I guess that's all right. I'm currently involved in conducting fascinating scientific research and could use all the help I can get.

I'm Yaver Tul and I'm conducting research on military applications. And presently I'm in dire need of a hero like you.
I've been told there are massive gars in the Hissing Canyon. Their mandibles look so formidable that I wouldn't risk coming close to them for the all treasures in the Universe!
But you aren't afraid of some ugly bugs, are you?
The point is that the crawlers' mandibles contain a special thick liquid. Incidentally, it's almost an ideal solvent, though that's irrelevant.
The gars' plates are very light, sturdy, flexible, and tough as a sheet of steel! It's a pity I have only a few samples. If I want to perform more serious research, I will obviously need more. I know that if I had more shields, I could invent a brand new type of armor!
Well, how are the crawlers doing? Still breathing? I hope you will fix that soon.

Wow! That's really strong! A shield like this is truly priceless!
And the mandibles are full of potent acid. One drop will eat through a breastplate. It's just what I needed!
Participate in killing Rocktooth and bring its breastplate to Yaver Tul at the researchers' camp by the entrance to the wormface cave.

I can only make light armor out the plates I have. Tough as they are, they are still far too fragile for a heavy breastplate. A few strong blows would be enough to crack them.
I need something stronger... Like the plates of a very mature gar.
I saw one like it in the depths of the Hissing Canyon. A horrible beast! I don't think you can kill him on your own. But if you're not alone... So gather your friends and go. Bring me its breastplate! My reward will be generous.
If I could make armor out of Rocktooth's breastplate, it will be a genuine masterpiece!

Wow! Now that's a plate! How did you manage to best a creature with such a thick hide? Then again, I don't particularly care about that. The important thing is that you did it, and in doing so you've earned this reward.
Now I'm going to start tinkering with fittings. Who knows, perhaps soon all military weapons and armor will bear my brand!
Meet with Kirill Pryatkin in the wormface cave on the Island of Revelation.

Keeper of the Revelation! Don't be surprised - now that you know the Truth, this title is rightfully yours. I have an important errand for you.
You already know that wormfaces have betrayed us and the Master. Well, in doing so they have also signed their own death warrant. Their actions have effectively nullified all rules and agreements that were in effect. Including the agreement restricting surface inhabitants from going down into their cave.
A seasoned scout named Kirill Pryatkin was sent down there, but I'm afraid there's no way he can do the job all alone.
Go into the wormface cave and locate Kirill, and the two of you can decide on the best course of action. The more damage you cause to the enemy now, the less trouble they'll be to us later.
Hey, you! Psst... Come here. Be quiet, those tentacle-faced beasts have keen hearing.
Search the draconid remains and take everything that might be used to destroy the Keepers, then report your findings to Kirill Pryatkin.

I heard about you from my sister. Do your remember her? She says your help at the Dragon Ring proved quite useful. I trust my sister and therefore I trust you.
Now listen carefully. There aren't that many wormfaces left here in the cave. Most of them have gone off somewhere deep into the Misty Lands. The ones who stayed behind are mainly scientists, researchers and Keepers. And I want to talk to you about the Keepers.
They differ considerably from regular wormfaces. Not only are they taller and considerably stronger, their greatest distinction is their magic. They can boil your brains right inside your head!
And yet I've seen draconids sneak into the cave and kill Keepers outright. Granted, they didn't survive themselves, but it's interesting to note that Keepers can, in fact, be killed. No, not "can be" - must be!
Look around. Perhaps you'll be able to find out how the draconids managed to wipe out so many wormfaces. If I were you, I would start by searching the bodies of the dead draconids and the nearby items. I'll be right behind you. But don't expect me to help in combat - I am a scout, not a warrior. If I could cut through enemies by the dozen, I'd do it without you.
Well, did you find anything valuable?

This is quite an unusual stone. I've seen its kind before. Remember the "kaboomers" that were used to blow up demonic portals on the Twilight Isle? Well, kaboomers are actually made out of plain-looking stones like this one. The draconids call them thunderstones. When thrown they explode with a super-bright flare. And it appears that the flare blinds the Keepers, so that they become completely defenseless. Interesting, yes? And certainly useful.
Destroy a Keeper using a thunderstone, and signal Kirill Pryatkin with the signal lamp.

These days it's the Keepers that pose the greatest threat to us. If you kill enough Keepers, other wormfaces will be disorganized and won't put up much of a resistance. But there's a problem: killing a Keeper is far from easy.
However, there's a way. This thunderstone here. Its flare can literally burn the Keeper's eyes out, since they're only used to subterranean darkness. And then you should have no trouble killing him!
I'll give you a signal lamp. It has a very narrow beam that can hardly be seen from a distance. If you need me, give me a signal by flashing the light three times
I saw an explosion in the depths of the cave and heard sounds of battle. Is the Keeper dead?

Hehehe, I bet the Keeper can now be swept into a dustpan and kept in a fist-size box, right? Great!
And he had this bottle with acid on him? Don't be in a rush to thrash it. I reckon we can use any information, technology, weapons and materials used by wormfaces in this war.
I heard explosions in the depths of the cave. Are the Keepers dead?

Hehehe, judging by the racket, I bet the Keeper can now be swept into a dustpan and kept in a fist-size box, right? Great!
And the acid on them may just prove useful. Don't be in a rush to thrash it.
Report on the elimination of the wormface threat to the Keeper of Power at the Master's Citadel.

You've won a glorious victory today, my friend! I'm certain that the Keeper's death has had great impact on all wormfaces. And I'm even more certain that the cave inhabitants will have other things besides us to worry about in the near future.
Go to the Citadel and report to the Keeper of Power this delightful news! And take care of yourself. The wormfaces may be down, but they're not out. And after a while they'll surely be a nuisance again. So be sure to drop by later. I'll brief you on the current events, and together we'll think of more ways to frustrate our enemies.

That's really great news! While there's discord and friction among the wormfaces, they pose no threat to us.
Now we ought to shift out focus to draconids. If we deal with them, half of our problems will be solved!

They are way too many of those tentacle-faced freakshows for my liking... And with their excellent engineering and psionic abilities, they can wreak enormous damage should they decide to attack the Citadel. Ugh, how I hate fighting on three fronts! Wormfaces on one side, draconids on the other, all the while demons and cultists are operating their own island.
Well, what we can do is focus on eliminating at least one threat, and that's the wormfaces. They're so afraid of death you'd think they're planning to live forever. If we kill a score of them, the others will simmer down in no time!
They're disgusting, those wormfaces. It's obvious that we won't come to an agreement. Why did we even bother?

You're taking the old road through the ruins to get to the Outpost, right? Then keep your eyes open! A whole gang of draconids has settled there! They're as wicked as Cake when he gets hung over. Their teeth are this big! We barely managed to escape them.
We were using the road to deliver provisions, but now that those bastards are there we have no choice but to transport everything by water. The lake is wet and dangerous, and you feel like the boat will overturn at any moment...
So, listen, we need a favor. Beat the snot out of the draconids when you run into them. Damn goons shouldn't be lusting after our supplies. If you do it, all of our soldiers will be mighty grateful!
Hey, soldier, you don't look so good! Just out of combat, eh?

So you gave the draconids in the ruins a good beating? That's good, hehe! I'd challenge them myself, but who's gong to stay in command? No, I can't leave the post! I need to maintain discipline and cultivate productivity among my subordinates. Everything is pursuant to regulations!
Hey? What do you want? Bugs? What friggin' bugs? Are you high? I don't know nothin' about no bugs!

Is that right... So now we can see half the island in detail without having to raise our asses off the stool? Whoa, the Watchfulls sure are something else! Granted, they deserve an undressing for their... whatchamacallit... ill-advised initiative! But seeing as things worked out so well with the bugs and the squinteyes , I will instead thank you both!
I wonder what would happen if you planted such a bug in a ladies' bathhouse? Hey, that's not a bad idea!
Go to the Tuk-Miktu Ruins and find out the location of the recent battle.

Listen up. Last night, I decided to take a leak outside the Outpost's perimeter. Sometimes you just need some privacy, you know? So anyway, I was just standing there, bothering no one. The breeze was pleasant, the crickets were singing, the creek was bubbling... It was paradise!
And then came a huge explosion over the Tuk-Miktu Ruins to the south! Kaboom! I couldn't help but duck and cover! And then I heard sounds of a vicious battle coming from that direction. The wind carried much of the sounds loud and clear. Draconids shouting, fireballs raging, and some kind of round and blazing thing swishing through the air. The racket lasted for a few minutes and then died down just as suddenly.
I wanted to send my scouts there, but they're all already standing their watch. You're my only hope! Go there quietly and find out what happened. But watch your back. There are more draconids in there than my grandpa has war medals!
This draconid was unlucky... He looks as though he was trampled by a squad of war rhinos.
Go to the Tuk-Miktu Ruins and find out the location of the recent battle.

Listen up. Last night, I decided to take a leak outside the Outpost's perimeter. Sometimes you just need some privacy, you know? So anyway, I was just standing there, bothering no one. The breeze was pleasant, the crickets were singing, the creek was bubbling... It was paradise!

The wind carried much of the sounds loud and clear. Draconids shouting, fireballs raging, and some kind of round and blazing thing swishing through the air. The racket lasted for a few minutes and then died down just as suddenly.

This draconid was unlucky... He looks as though he was trampled by a squad of war rhinos.
Follow the strange bloody tracks to find the draconid's killer.

The draconid's body is torn to pieces, and it looks as if death came quite recently. The nature of the injuries is unsettling - never before have you seen a weapon that could inflict such horrible wounds. It looks almost as if someone tried to skewer the draconid alive.
To his credit, the draconid put up a desperate resistance. Suddenly you notice strange tracks. Looks like the battle took place elsewhere. The dying draconid managed to grab hold of his enemy and was dragged a few meters. Lightly phosphorescent liquid stains appear to be leading toward the demolished tower to the north. You should follow the tracks to find out which creature attacked the draconid. Perhaps the creature could become an ally?
I... knew... I cannot... beat... you...

Dying at the hand of... The strongest... is no shame...
There's great... power... behind you... It's generous to those... who... can understand... its... essence..
You... call it... a Patron... That is incorrect... With time... you'll understand...
Pay me one last... honor... Take my mask... Let this... be... your... trophy...
Fa... farewell...
Show the Destroyer's Mask to Semer Shabas at the Outpost.

What an interesting mask! You haven't seen anything like this technology even in the wormface cave on the Island of Revelation. Its metal is unbelievably light and extremely tough, and it is entirely unknown to you, though it bears some resemblance to blued steel. And inside the mask you're looking at extremely fine mechanisms...
Perhaps you should show this mask to Semer Shabas. After all, who else but a Zem scientist could make sense of alien technology?
Why are you disturbing me? Can't you see I'm busy?

Hrm... So it was a kind of wormface you've never seen before, and he materialized out of thin air? He said something about the Patrons and gave you his mask as a trophy? Interesting, very interesting...
We've already had a few encounters with the creatures you've described. Oh, they are formidable warriors, indeed! Silent, inconspicuous and extremely dangerous! And every of them opted to blow himself up rather than be captured. You're damn lucky that one of these Destroyers deigned to even speak to you. But since he did, perhaps that means you could also master their weapon? We've captured a few trophies, but the weapons all have some strange magic placed on them. They're no more dangerous in the hands of our warriors than a toothpick, though the Destroyers used them to exterminate a whole squad of draconids right in front of our scouts in mere seconds.
But you should go see our expert armorer Yaver Arafi if you want to know more about this weapon. Now go and leave me be. I need to think.
Test the Destroyer's spear on a draconid and on a golem, then report the results to Yaver Arafi at the Outpost.

I'll give you one of our trophies. Four of our best soldiers and a fellow researcher have perished to acquire this spear. When our fighters finally managed to disarm the wormface, the spear turned into a harmless metal pole! But I saw with my own eyes the Destroyer run that spear through steel armor as if it were a sheet of parchment.
Take the spear and test it... Say, on a golem and on a draconid. You see, I have a theory that the spear is "tuned" to fight certain types of enemies. And if my theory is true...
But it's too early to draw conclusions just yet. First we need to know the result, whatever it is.
This weapon is probably the strangest thing I've seen in my long lifetime, both before and after death.
Hrm. So the spear that skewered the draconid as if it'd been a duck didn't even graze the golem? Looks like my theory is being confirmed.
Test the Destroyer's chakram on a draconid and on a golem, then report results to Yaver Arafi at the Outpost.

And here is another trophy, a throwing disk that belonged to one of the Destroyers. This is a very rare weapon that requires exceptional skill to handle. These disks are called chakram. Its distinctive feature lies in always returning to its owner after it is thrown. We're very lucky to have gotten hold of this chakram. Of course, the actual soldier who had "gotten hold" of it wasn't so lucky... Take this chakram and test it on draconids and golems. I wonder how the weapon will react.
I hope you won't chop off your fingers or your head with this chakram.
I was right! The weapon cuts through draconids with ease yet it's totally useless against golems. I guess the saying is true: "dog does not eat dog."
Equip the Destroyer's mask and tell Yaver Arafi what you feel.

The last thing we must do is test the mask itself. Frankly, I am... scared. I don't even know what metal it is made of, never mind all the other questions. I have absolutely no clue what might happen if you put it on. I only hope you won't turn into a Destroyer yourself. Hah!
Anyway, I don't think the Destroyer gave you his mask to kill you. So come on! Equip the mask and tell me what you feel.

Well, well, well... My theory is confirmed. The mask is obviously made to easily operate on the surface both during the day and at night. Wormfaces have very sensitive eyes that cannot bear sunlight. The mask allows them to see in a different spectrum, to feel the creatures' body heat or magic auras. And I bet this mask allows its wearer to see through the veil of invisibility that conceals Destroyers! So there's one use for your trophy. Do you follow?
Find the Destroyers and return to Semer Shabas at the Outpost. You should search in the vicinities of the Rotten Creek, the Tuk-Miktu Ruins and the Ancient Portal.

Oh yes, I've already heard of your feats and Yaver Arafi's theory. And I agree with him. There's only one thing I don't understand...
Look, we found out that these "Destroyers" are purposefully exterminating draconids. Judging by their considerable progress, they've been warring for over a decade. This raises a question: What did the Destroyer see in you to give you his mask? Perhaps it's because you've won the trust of both the draconids and the wormfaces. You've even managed to stop their endless war for a while... I don't know. But I want to know as much as you do!
And your trophy will help us. Equip the mask, switch on thermal vision and go seek out the Destroyers. They're not going to attack you... At least I hope they won't. I think they're drawn to the ancient ruins. Look for their tracks near the Rotten Creek, the Tuk-Miktu Ruins and the Ancient Portal.
I hope you're not distracting me out of idle curiosity?
Ah, I was right! The Destroyers did not harm you! And you say they actually invited you to meet their elder and undergo a trial by combat? Holy cow...
Meet the Destroyers' Leader in the Dusty Ruins and defeat all Destroyer contenders.

A duel... Well, I don't doubt your abilities. You have enough power to best any enemy. But is it in you to comprehend the kind of power that stands behind the Destroyers? Or the source of their strange magic? Or what the hell they even are?! Well, let's hope your mind is as sharp as your blade.
Go to the Dusty Ruins and show these Destroyers that they're not the only good fighters around!

You've defeated each of my younger brothers. Truly, that is a heroic feat. I never thought it was possible...
The power that your people call "Patron" has imparted onto you a generous portion of its own might. But I also sense something that my eyes cannot quite see...
Return to the Outpost and tell Semer Shabas about what you have seen.

Listen to me, stranger, for I, Kaid, never waste time. Do you think we met by chance? No. Fate itself brought you here. Fate and what you surface dwellers call a "patron." I feel the power brimming within both you and me! And this power comes from the same source.
But my race does not believe in any "patrons"! I chanced to hear about some of your sorcerers who died ages ago. It is said that their Sparks had dissolved in the astral and became what people now call "Patrons." But look at me! My brothers and I are endowed with the same power as you. The fact that you mastered our weapons only proves this. Now think, why would spellcasters from the surface endow underground creatures like us with what appears to be their own power? Why so silent? You don't know what to say? I don't either...
All I know is that there is a mystical power in our world. We call this power the Source. You call it Patrons. Our Source has twelve manifestations, twelve faces. You have twelve Patrons. This power gives you the ability to heal yourself, fight pain and fear, become stronger or more accurate... We cannot do these things. But with the same power we can become invisible, see what is hidden and feel what is concealed... and many things that the surface creatures couldn't even begin to fathom.
Don't let my frankness surprise you. The power of the Source has brought you here, and chose me to be the conductor of its will. I told you much of what we know. Not everything, but quite a lot! Consider it my gift to you for your valor in combat. And now we must part. Remember that our races are enemies. Should fate reunite us on the battlefield, I will not hesitate to kill you, nor will I regret it.

I... We... This is... I just don't know what to say! This is incredible! It just cannot be! Look, I already know that the wormfaces used to be Junes. Still, our Patrons are our Patrons! Why would they endow their powers to some underground worms? Besides, if this Kaid character is to be trusted, their powers are radically different from ours. This is very strange...
Either this wormface is a brilliant actor, capable of deceiving even the Purgatory goblin, or everything we know about the Patrons is wrong! But that means the records, the legends... Not to mention our scientific theses and laboratory research studies! I simply cannot fathom it... This is some food for thought, indeed. And I hope you manage to crack the mystery.

You... How do you know about the Destroyers' relic? Now you will not escape death. Even if you win this combat, other Destroyers will come and kill you. But I, Kaid, promised to answer your question and I will keep my word. The Bowl is in our Temple. It connects us with our origins and gives us strength which is unattainable for the mortals. Only those who prove to be worthy can touch it. And you are not one of them.

Prepare to die!
h: Ask about the Bowl of Origins

t: You have to fight three of my disciples and defeat each of them. But that alone will not be enough. By besting each of my disciples you will only prove that speaking to you now is not a total waste of my time. But if you show me a real fighter's spirit and swagger, perhaps I might deign to actually continue this conversation.
Return to the Outpost and tell Semer Shabas about what you have seen.

The fact that you mastered our weapons only proves this. Now think, why would spellcasters from the surface endow underground creatures like us with what appears to be their own power? Why so silent? You don't know what to say? I don't either...
All I know is that there is a mystical power in our world. We call this power the Source. You call it Patrons. Our Source has twelve manifestations, twelve faces. You have twelve Patrons. This power gives you the ability to heal yourself, fight pain and fear, become stronger or more accurate... We cannot do these things. But with the same power we can become invisible, see what is hidden and feel what is concealed... and many things that the surface creatures couldn't even begin to fathom.
Don't let my frankness surprise you. The power of the Source has brought you here, and chose me to be the conductor of its will. I told you much of what we know. Not everything, but quite a lot! Consider it my gift to you for your valor in combat. And now we must part. Remember that our races are enemies. Should fate reunite us on the battlefield, I will not hesitate to kill you, nor will I regret it.

I... We... This is... I just don't know what to say! This is incredible! It just cannot be! Look, I already know that the wormfaces used to be Junes. Still, our Patrons are our Patrons! Why would they endow their powers to some underground worms? Besides, if this Kaid character is to be trusted, their powers are radically different from ours. This is very strange...
Either this wormface is a brilliant actor, capable of deceiving even the Purgatory goblin, or everything we know about the Patrons is wrong! But that means the records, the legends... Not to mention our scientific theses and laboratory research studies! I simply cannot fathom it... This is some food for thought, indeed. And I hope you manage to crack the mystery.
Participate in killing the Draconid Queen and bring her head to Kaid in the Dusty Ruins.

Your victory looked... reassuring to me and my brothers. We Destroyers are endowed with a special gift. Our vow and our code bid us to use our power for one purpose only - to destroy creatures that breed like locust. I'm talking about the draconids! It wasn't long that the world didn't even know about them. And in just a few years their numbers have exploded to a point where they are primed to overwhelm the whole world, their scaly flesh sweeping away everyone and everything like an avalanche. But I, Kaid, vow that this shall never happen! We shall destroy these despicable creatures and their false god they call the Fiery Father. And we propose to you to join us in this war. Your aid will not make us friends for as long as you serve the traitor. But the war against surface dwellers is not our war. We only fight the draconids and their allies.
My brothers have found a nest on the Smoldering Highland. And not just any nest, but the queen's nest! It is guarded by the giant draconid queen, and I fear to imagine what might hatch from those eggs.
Bring me her head and I shall reward you handsomely. Have no doubt that by destroying that creature before she breeds a swarm of cold-blooded killers, you will be doing a good deed. But bear in mind that this queen is stronger than all of my brothers combined. To best her you will need a strong team.
One day we shall live on the surface once again, unburdened by the heavy armor that protects me and my brothers from the scorching sun... And woe to anyone who might try to drive us back underground!

The Queen is dead? That's great news! Alas, some other draconid will soon her place soon... The draconids procreate like wild beasts. Well, they are beasts, after all. And each destroyed nest is a step towards the triumph of reason throughout the world.
I promised you a reward and I shall keep my word!
Meet the Master's Voice in the Citadel.

Well, now you know... quite a lot. Not all there is to know, but what I've told you is more than enough. The vast majority of living things live long and utterly blind lives without ever learning even a tiny fraction of what you now know. For now, I have nothing more to tell you. Later, perhaps.
Now go to my faithful servant. What does he call himself? Ah, yes - the Master's Voice... Well, that can't be helped - there is a measure of theatrics inherent to my creatures. Every single one of them believes they've been chosen by the gods!
In short, go to the Master's Voice. It will fill you in on the details.
Finally! I've been waiting for you!
Eliminate the draconid and wormface threats, then return to the Master's Voice at the Citadel.

We shall annihilate the traitors! We will wipe them from the face of the earth! If you are loyal to the Master, if your heart is repulsed by treachery, as is mine, then you can help us.
Go seek out the Keepers of the Altar of Truth. They will explain the plan to protect the Citadel from our former allies. Follow their instructions as if they came from the Master himself! Return to me once you've dealt with our foes on Draconid Island and in the Wormface Cave.
We cannot engage in an all-out battle for as long as traitors are threatening the Citadel. Hurry up!

Your reputation precedes you.
With our enemies defeated, the Citadel is safe. It's time you headed for the Frontier!

Go to the Frontier and find the lair of the giant underground worm. Lure him out of his burrow with Rocktooth's blood. Vanquish the worm, and report to George Siverian, who will be waiting for you near the Master's Citadel.

Hmm... Very interesting. I might even say you lucked out. Although, in your place I wouldn't be too quick to celebrate.
The other day I heard one of the mercenaries say that there's fighting on the Frontier, and something about a huge, cave-dwelling worm. Its maw is so massive it could swallow an orc whole without a hiccup! It's got teeth like fine knives, as long as your arm! Its hide is as thick as a stout beam. Oy... That'd be the trophy to end all trophies.
But I can't just drop everything and head for the Frontier! You see, I've had a dust-up with some local mercenaries. One thing led to another, I banged my fist on the table, and... Basically, the timing's not right for me to travel. But if you want to make some money, go find that worm. That vile thing's probably got his burrow somewhere in the foothills. Look for gnawed bones, broken weapons, and scraps of armor. And it'll reek so bad your eyes will burn! A creature like that eats a lot and craps even more.
Once you find him, sprinkle some gar's blood on the dirt. The smell will draw the beast out. But don't even think about taking him on alone. Gather some friends, and not just one or two but a whole brigade, at least. Only then test your fate in combat with the worm.
What tidings do you bring - good or ill?

Good lord! I can't believe it! Don't bother, I've already heard the story of your battle with the giant worm. I burn with envy! Such a victory will no doubt inspire my good friend Vasya the Cornflower to compose a ballad! Of course, he does write ballads at the drop of a hat. At least this one will be about fighting. Ah! I promised you a prize! Would a song do? A song might bear your name for centuries! No? Then take your prize. George Siverian's word is his bond!
Take a clot of Rocktooth's blood to George Siverian.

The blood trickling from the body of the slain Rocktooth is giving off a stunning pong, something sour and coppery. If regular gar blood attracts ordinary earthworms, then what kind of monster will this stuff bring out?
Maybe you should get a word of advice from George. He's hunted a few monsters in his day.

Yuck! What a stench! Is that you? Ugh... Don't stand upwind, you smelly bastard, my eyes are burning.
Wait, what? It's not you, it's the flask? Let's see what you've got there.
Meet the Master's Voice in the Citadel.

Hey, where are you off to? Trying to get on the ship? Stop!
Do you want to die? We're fighting draconids! They'll torch your ship before you even get close, and you'll be cremated before you hit the ground! If you want to reach the island, go to the Master's Voice. He will help you.
Damned drakes! They have already torched almost a dozen of our astral ships!

Those ignorant drakes think we can't get to the island without a ship. It's as if they're oblivious to the portal's existence. All the worse for them! Let me know if you want to visit their island. I'll get you there.

Greetings, Seeker of Truth. I see doubt in your eyes.
What bothers you?
I understand your concerns. No, I haven't seen the people you describe. I doubt they are that brave or that stupid to approach the Citadel after they refused to follow the Master's law.
Report all this to Gammon the Tempestuous. He's waiting for you at the outpost.

It turns out that neither the draconids nor the wormfaces ever trusted Nihaz. In fact, they'd been plotting against him for a while. Biding their time, they distracted the Master and then struck when the timing suited. Their goal is the Dead City. It's not so much the town they're after, but there's something hidden there, some kind of a powerful artifact that the Overmind, Nihaz, and the Fiery Father all want. I'm worried that we'll never learn anything until we head to the Dead City to see all this with our own eyes.
Go to the outpost, find Gammon, and tell him what we know. He's dumb as a chunk of meat, but he can get the information where it needs to go. Better to have the League and the Empire know what Nihaz and our former allies are planning. It seems to me that all the strange things happening here in the Misty Lands are eventually going to reach the outside world.

And were you able to find this spying little pissant? Good, let her keep crawling. Or else she'll spoil my discipline with her dubious morals. When would you ever see a commanding officer contradicted in front of subordinates? Better to be a... what d'ye call it... a mercenary. Hah!
But don't worry, I'll pass the information along. Let those city bureaucrats worry about all that bollocks. We've enough to do as it is.
Find Ekaterina Drabova in the eastern reaches of the Frontier.

Listen, you. We had a whole squad of Kanians here. They were led by this warrior broad, Ekaterina Drabova. Imagine: a whole ladies' battalion! What a treat!
Where was I? Ah yes. The Kanians left for the eastern shore. Probably trying to establish a base there. They took over some old June relic, a something-or-other. They fixed it up, and then used it to link up with our teleporter at the outpost. Not good enough to transport people, but cargo and such. And you could send messages.
Till the other day, when they just dropped off the face of the earth. And that thing of theirs quit working - no signal. Quit mucking about and go and see what's what! Just don't kill all the bad guys, save some for us, eh?
Stop! One more step and I'll shoot without warning... Hey, you're one of ours! Great! Someone's finally come to see what we've got going on here.
Destroy eight June Monoliths, then report to Ekaterina Drabova upon completion.

Wait till I get my hands on that Gammon... I'll turn that meathead into a proper sausage... We've been stuck here for days, cut off from everything, and that lout didn't move a muscle! What do you expect from an orc?
In any case, we're glad to see you! Just in time, too.
We fixed an old June teleporter. You can't transport people with it, but cargo is a snap. Food, water, weapons, ammunition... If it wasn't for the wormfaces!
I guess there used to be a whole set of teleporters here, or something along those lines. The wormfaces rearranged some of the monoliths that were left over from other teleporters, and now I can't even send a scrap of paper, thanks to disruptions in the magical plane. We were ready to forget it all and head back to the outpost, but it's a different story now that you've arrived! If we destroy the old monoliths the connection with the outpost will be restored.
I knew you'd do all right. We're back online with the outpost, and now we can get everything we need using the teleporter. Thanks much!
Make your way to the ancient portal and take a better look at the portal guard. Then return to Ekaterina Drabova to make your report.

Well, now our camp is safe. And I've just received a message. And it concerns you. We need to learn more about these ancient gates and the army of wormfaces.
There's a bit of dry land to the east of here. On it you'll find a strange construction, and odds are those are the ancient gates in question. There's a bridge out to the island, and it's guarded by golems. But they're not the issue! The issue is the giant golem that guards the gates themselves. I've no idea what to do about that big galloot.
I know what Gannon would want to do, but you can't defeat a guard like that by brute force alone. We need to be clever. It's like the joke about the mechanic working on the astral ship engine: "You paid me one gold piece to hit the engine with a hammer, and the other fifty you paid was for knowing where to hit."
We, too, must know where to hit. Sneak your way or blast your way across the bridge and get a closer look at the guard. He must have a weak spot!
I wish those golems would crumble to dust! We've had nothing but trouble from this "June heritage"...

You say there's a golem there protected by a force field? Like a supercharged version of the shields on astral ships? Something on the level of the Aegis, or even better? The wormfaces sure can pick ‘em... Sounds like a tough bastard.
But we're no lightweights, are we? Look, the shields on astral ships shatter under fire from astral weapons, right? So why can't we destroy the golem's shield with our cannons?
Meet with Gammon the Tempestuous at the Outpost.

This is how we'll do it. Go back to the outpost and talk to Gammon. Tell him everything that we learned, and try to think of a way to get past the golem to the portal. Something makes me reluctant to take on that big bruiser. If fact, I don't even have the time to plan an attack on the portal right now.
Gammon doesn't have much for brains, but he's got more advisors than you can shake a stick at. Maybe you'll come up with something together.

The portal? A burly golem? No, I don't know anything about such things.
You should talk to some of our smarter fellas. They already spend all their time in their laboratories. Let them earn their keep for once! Hah!
Get the key to the ancient portal by defeating Ram Shaitan, the ancient war golem. To defeat the golem's shield you'll need to use the cannons on the shore.

Look, our brainiacs have been thinking. And they've come up with something!
You'll need a key to get to the portal. It'll be made of June plastic and covered with symbols. It's like you're one of ours, see? The golem serves the wormfaces. He lets them through freely and uses the key to open the portal. You won't be able to get through without the key. Like it or not, you'll have to take out the golem. It won't be an easy task. He's a tough one, tough like my mum. But we've dealt with bigger ones. Ekaterina's troops have set up their artillery along the shore. A couple of shells from those cannons and he's a goner! Hah! But you can't do it alone. Someone's got to distract the golem and someone else has to be on the cannons. So get together a posse and go for it! Get that key!

All that work for a piddling piece of plastic... I'll never understand it.
Now that you've got the key, you can continue on without any trouble. Use the key near that big stone lout and he won't touch you.
the Dead City awaits... I wish I could take your place... But I have to be here. Without me, the wormfaces and scalies would have the run of the place! Hah!
If we were big like orcs, we wouldn't need any of this garbage, we'd just grind ‘em into sausage meat with our bare hands...
Oh! Barrels! They look just like beer casks... Is there beer inside? Are the insides bubbling? No? Too bad! Beer would be nice right now, and some fish jerky... But you did good! Many thanks!
Escort the sapper to the right spot in the Wild Rocks and wait for him to blow up the cliff over the cave. Then return to the Watchfull family at the docks.

Hey! Greetings! We've got another bit of work for you! You're going to like it!
Remember the barrels of explosives? Well, we found a way to use them. An outpost egghead who messes around with gadgets sent us a new guard recently. A mechanical one! It's as dumb as... as... well, he's dumber than our Cake, let's put it that way. And he's just as buttoned up, too. There's no one at all to talk to here, other than you...
At least we've got that dumb bu... what did we call him? Ah well, it doesn't matter. We're going to have our own suicide bomber! That metal lunkhead won't be good for much else, anyway. We've loaded him up with all the explosives. Now he's set to blow up on command! And he'll bury that cave.
Oh, and we forgot to tell you the most important part! We want to collapse the cave where the wormfaces live. If you take the path up to the Wild Rocks, you'll end up right over the entrance to the cave. A big explosion on that spot would collapse the cave. And the wormfaces will have to dig a new entrance. Pretty good plan, eh?
We're giving you the job of escorting our sapper. Follow him until he gets to the spot. There will surely be armed resistance for our ‘Wind of Death' operation. But you're not scared of wormfaces or draconids, are you? You can help, right? It will be hard to beat the drakes and protect the sapper all by yourself. Call some of your friends to help.
And we'll give you this, just in case - a magic shield generator. It gives the sapper temporary protection against enemies.
One more thing. As soon as the sapper is in position and the countdown begins, get out of there as fast as you can. Otherwise, we'll be gathering you up all over the astral!
I wonder how long the wormfaces will need to dig a new tunnel. We think it'll take them a good couple of days, at least!

Whoa! That was quite the blast! We even saw it from here!
Those wormfaces under there must be boiling!
Repel the attack on the Outpost and protect Semyon Dyldin at all costs. When you're done, report to Gammon the Tempestuous.

Just in time! The enemy's getting ready to attack our outpost! The draconids and wormfaces have had a falling out, and we've ended up piggy in the middle. This is twice as bad as if they'd attacked us separately.
I've just learned that the two armies are going to meet at a certain time in the same field that we set up our outpost. This time is noted on your calendar. Strike me dead, but we need everyone who can carry an axe!
Do you see that beanpole? The one as big and tough as my grandmum? That's Semyon Dyldin. He's going to lead our defenders. Not because he's smart - I'm the smart one around here. Who do you think is going to be the first mark? The biggest one! He's going to lead all our attacks. Stay close, though, OK?
Your job is to help Semyon. Otherwise they'll have his head in less than an hour. And where would I find another lummox like him? So come on, don't be shy! Destroy the scalies and wormfaces!
And that... Well, they've promised reinforcements in case things here go haywire... But they're late, damn it! The teleporter is a little glitchy, but it's working. So, uh... Wander around the camp a bit, go see the ruins. Looks like those greasy slimefaces are blocking our portal with their monoliths. Find the monoliths and blast them to smithereens! Otherwise, without help, we're doomed.

Phew. I thought we were done for. We barely got out alive! Now the scaly beasts have gone all quiet... Too bad it won't be for long! I hope they choke on a boot! Come back tomorrow, if your sword's thirsty! We'll have a fight! Hah!
If those draconids hadn't reproduced so quickly, we'd have wiped them from the allods a long time ago!
Enter the portal at the Frontier.

Now that you have a key you can continue on. You'll know what to do once you get close to that stone monster. The magic in the key will help you neutralize the Keeper.
the Dead City awaits... I wish I could take your place... But I have to be here. Otherwise the wormfaces and scalies would have the run of the place! Haw!
Well, it's been fun. Take care of yourself! Don't forget old Gammon! Stop by if you need anything.
Sarn's demons are offering us a pact? That's amusing.

Lies and deception can sometimes sound sweet, but don't be fooled! Sarn's adepts are suicidal maniacs. They hate this world and are constantly trying to destroy it. Don't ever forget it. Anyway... I suppose I'll accept their offer!
It's been so long since Light and Dark have worked together. This will be an interesting game, let me tell you. Hehe.
Go to the Wandering Island and talk to Patriarch Semer Knef in the cultists' camp.

Sarn is trying to get around me, to leave me behind... He'll pay for it... For the moment we share interests... for the moment. The wormfaces and draconids, those dirty traitors, decided to play rebels. I'll just have to punish the imbeciles. Under no circumstances can I allow them to enter the Dead City!
What do I see when I happen to turn my gaze to that corner of the astral? The path through the portal has been blocked by some unknown allod. The Wandering Island... Another shard of Gipat hidden beneath ancient ruins. The wormfaces and draconids are already there and, if my eyes do not deceive, they are beelining towards the portal. That's right, the Wandering Island has another portal. And this portal also leads to the Dead City.
But not only have you fallen behind the traitors, the demon worshippers are ahead of you as well... I'm talking about Sarn cultists. All they do is sit shaking in their camp like a herd of sheep. These sycophants of Sarn are helpless, they can't even clear their own path.
Go to them and let them carry out the wishes of their beloved god, if it means they'll help us stop those traitors! And see that you don't get lost. It's always nice to do your dirty work with someone else's hands.
Another one of Nihaz's minions. Did the Radiant Sarn speak with you?

Don't ever forget this moment! The Creator showed you the way and even deigned to speak with you. It's rare for a non-believer to be graced with such an honor. You can't even fathom what an opportunity this is, unworthy creation of Sarn.
Take the Oath of Light with Semer Knef at the cultists' camp.

This is a holy war! We didn't allow you to stand shoulder to shoulder with us right away. If you want to fight under the banners of the Light, then first swear the Oath of Light to our All-Merciful Savior.
Swear, too, your allegiance to the tribe of demons, that most exquisite, most youthful, most perfect creation of the Radiant Sarn. For many centuries, Sarnaut's crude creations have failed to understand this. We endured so much before the simple truth was revealed to us - one must not fight demons, one should serve them!
Put your hand on your heart. May the astral swallow you up if you ever break the Oath! I am ready to listen.

The Oath of Light is not the easiest step on your path to the Truth and away from the lies of the Master of Darkness. It is only your first step on the path to the Truth, where many tests and trials still await.

It was the wisdom of the Great Sarn that brought us here. Good thing, too...
There is a bloody battle underway for this island, which is littered with the remnants of a once great city. Every fighter is accounted for!
Talk to the cultists' leader, Dmitri Gromov, and the demons' leader, Goliath, at the cultists' camp. Then return to Father Semer Knef.

The enemies of the Light have taken all the important positions. The attacks never cease, day or night. But all of our attempts have been futile! Every time we make the slightest advance, the enemy responds and we are driven back. Our soldiers are losing heart, and even the commanders have stopped charging into battle with any vigor. I summoned all the courage of the Light, all the inspiration of the holy spirit, to no avail. I have given up, to tell you the truth. Many of our kind hate you, my friend. Many of our fighters would gladly kill you if it weren't for our pact. But we've all heard of your military prowess! Your achievements truly demand respect.
That's why I wanted to ask you a favor. Talk to our commanders and find out what they think of our situation. The cultists' forces are led by Dmitri Gromov, while the demons follow Goliath.
Oh, Creator! Do not deny us your mercy. We need your host now more than ever!

Do you see what's happening with our commanders? Still, I do believe that there's hope. I can picture it now. Sarn didn't send you here for nothing. His ways are mysterious; I can only try to understand them. I think that you and your friends are just the ones to inspire our commanders, to fill their exhausted hearts anew with hope, and to lead by example. Remind them how to fight! Talk to our strategist, Punch the Furious.

Accept the Death to our Foe mission from Punch the Furious. Complete the Undead of Bone Hill mission. Read the report to any one of the commanders, join the attack and capture any of the enemy's camps. Then return to Semer Knef.

I'm sure you know that planning attacks is no easy task. When facing foes like the wormfaces or the draconids, any mistake, any deviation from the plan is as good as suicide!
Do you think you can handle any foe? We'll see.
First talk to our strategist, Punch the Furious. He's got an important mission for you that's related to our positions and plan of attack. Heed him well!
I, too, have an errand for you. The undead... No, I have nothing against the undead. I myself, in fact, am not entirely alive. But the undead spawning on Bone Hill are stupid, aggressive, and are a constant headache for our commanders.
Carry out this mission and you'll soon have a report that the undead have been defeated. Read your report to any commander. Every victory, no matter how minor, will raise the spirits of our soldiers. Then, once their spirits are at their peak, join the attack and take an enemy fortification.Note that you will become a part of the assault team only after reporting to a commander.
Prove that you're more than a hero of fable, but of life!
If only I were younger, say, closer to 150, I'd lead them into battle myself! Old age is no picnic, let me tell you. My knee's been acting up again...

The fortification is ours, just like that! We attacked with flawless grace and precision, it was like watching an orchestra follow sheet music. Excellent work!
I can see that the tales of your prowess were no exaggeration.
Capture three key points on the island: Swampy Pass, the Wretched Corner, and the Palace Square. When victorious, report to Punch the Furious at the cultists' camp.

Funtime is over! Enough standing around, picking your nose! The enemy had ample reinforcements and again we got a good drubbing. The wormfaces regained control of the Swampy Pass. The draconids, may they rot in the grave, are back at the Wretched Corner. All right, my hearties - to arms!
I remind you of our plan: Goliath and the demons are to take the Swampy Pass from the wormfaces. Gromov will take the Wretched Corner. Then the lot of us, coming from both sides, will attack the Palace Square and decimate the enemy positions.

Is something unclear? I'll repeat myself for those slow on the uptake. Gromov will drive the draconids from the Wretched Corner. Goliath will capture the Swampy Pass. Then we'll all descend upon the square, and that will be the end of them!

We showed them again! They're done for! And we've done it! Huzzah!
Here's your reward. But calm down a bit. You know that the enemy will be up in our beeswax again soon enough. The headaches never abate for long!
Are you tired? Alas, the only way to get any rest is to go home to mommy, head back to Nezebgrad, to Novograd, or board a ship. We've got a war going on here!
Earn 3 Seals of Sarn's Benevolence and give them to Father Semer Knef at the cultists' camp.

I accepted your Oath. I believe it wholeheartedly, but there's no better vow than that backed up by noble deeds. We, the forces of Light, the cultists of Sarn, have the most holy of missions - the destruction of the wormfaces and draconids. Mutants and degenerates are enemies of the Creator and nature itself. Fighting on our side, you will earn the highest awards that any cultist can aspire to: the Seal of Sarn's Benevolence. If you can gather enough of them we will understand that you are pure of heart, that you are fighting for the Light, and then we will help you find the path to the Wandering Island. That piece of land disrupted the portal connection, but we know how to find the road through the darkness. When the time comes, and if you can earn our trust, I'll show you the road.
One more thing. It's important to us that those on our side fight nobly, without lacking anything they need. During the fighting you'll be able to accumulate Seals of Sarn's Benevolence, which you can exchange at our traders for items that can be found nowhere else in Sarnaut.
Good fighting luck to you! May Sarn be with us!
Your efforts will not be wasted. We are watching you and we can see how much you do for the glory of the God of Light.
Oh! You've done the cult a significant service. We now have no doubt that you can be trusted. Sarn was so right to have chosen you and sent you here.
Once you've triggered the Stabilizer, enter the portal under the Palace Square.

I want to repay you for your service to us. I know you are trying to reach the Dead City... And we are in a position to help you. As you know, the ancient portal to the Dead City is highly unstable. It's been flickering, and jumping into a flickering portal is a good way to lose your Spark. But it's not all bad.
We've designed this portal stabilizer so that we could get more of our warriors through to the Dead City. Luckily for you, we haven't had a chance to use it yet. Now I'd like to give this priceless invention to you. Trigger the stabilizer before you approach the portal. If our calculations are correct, the way to the Dead City will open up ahead of you.
I have faith that the wisdom of Sarn will some day help you see the light. But don't forget that once we've left the boundaries of this island, those that trust the false god Nihaz will never know peace from us again.
What are you doing here? Was the Dead City too tough for you?

What is this? It can't be! The portal has closed and even the Stabilizer didn't help?
I don't even know what to tell you. I will pray heartily for the God of Light to tell us what to do. In the meantime, please accept this humble gift. It's the least I can do to repay you for your efforts.

You must join Goliath or Dmitri Gromov during the assault, then capture five key points on the island: Swampy Pass, Wretched Corner, and the Palace Square. When victorious, report to Punch the Furious at the cultists' camp.

So I'll explain our di... disposition. Well, "disposition" is just a fancy way of saying "where to go and who to kill." There are three places where the scum have dug in. The wormfaces have set up in the Swampy Pass. The scalies have taken over the Wretched Corner. Then, in the monsters' rear...(hehe) I mean, to the north is the Palace Square. The monsters' very lair! Devil only knows what we'll find there. But you don't need a fortuneteller to know it won't be good.
So we'll go hard. You, your friends, the cultists and demons... that's the only way we'll make it through. Goliath and the demons will chase the wormfaces out of the Swampy Pass. The cultists and Gromov will storm the Wretched Corner. Then we'll have to go kick the living... well, we'll attack the Square from all sides. Those are our orders. Got it? Sign here! Or at least scratch an X, if you can!
You will get a nice reward if you participate in capturing all check points!

Is something unclear? Let me say it again for those who are on a dreadnought. Goliath will drive the draconids from the Watchtower and the Wretched Corner. Gromov will capture the ruins and the Swampy Pass. Then we'll all descend upon the square, and that will be the end of them!

What, already? Victory is ours! Huzzah! We gave ‘em hell! I give everyone 24 hours to rest, drink, dress their wounds, find women... Then it starts again: up at 5 in the morning for drills. We can't let ourselves get weak. The enemy never rests.
Win the race by visiting every one of the Circles of Power on the track. The route: the Rotten Ruins, the Swampy Pass, the Palace Square, the Wretched Corner, the Watchtower, and the cultists' camp.

Ah, you're just in time. I've just come up with an experiment that could turn our understanding of modern science on its head!
You see, my area of research is the capabilities of Sparks outside the body. I need all the volunteers I can get. You will help me, won't you?
All I need you to do is to make you Spark leave the body and run the course I've laid out for you. That is, the Rotten Ruins then, through the Swampy Pass, to the Palace Square, then around the Wretched Corner to the Watchtower, and finish here, in the camp. It is simple as that, you have to enter the Circle of Power here and wait for the start signal. There is another Circle of Power like this one at each of the five points that you have to visit.
To give you some motivation along the way, we'll have a bit of a race: you'll be competing with other volunteers. Those that come in the top 3 will get a valuable prize!
So come here when it's time to race! The race schedule is on your calendar.
Hey you, how're you feeling? Nothing hurts? Great! My hypotheses were correct. We are on the brink of an amazing scientific discovery. Or, at least, I think we are.

Thanks for participating. The science appreciates your contribution. Maybe your name will be on my list of guinea pi... err, I mean, my assistants!
I'll send you your prize in the mail. That's it for now. You can relax. I need some time to analyze the data before we can repeat the race.

Our raiding the ruins and the tower is all well and good, but we best not forget about a much nearer threat! I'm talking about the Bone Hill undead. The last time they came around we gave 'em a real good thrashing, and they haven't been back since. But we ain't got the time to get up there regularly to remind them. Well, to this end we've got a test for greenhorns like you who are new to our cult.
Sarn is the God of Light, and light is hella fast. A split second and it's wherever it wants to be. No way you can catch up, no matter how fast your astral ship is. So let's test how fast you are! Here's the test: in a half-hour - no, a half-hour's a lot! Twenty five minutes! Twenty five minutes for you to kill thirty undead. That's right, thirty. Have you got the guts? Or are you too scared?

I should have wagered some money! I'd bet my shirt you're not going to make it! Unfortunately, the Patriarch ain't too keen on the idea, screeching about how important this is, that this is "a very important experiment done in the name of Sarn." I let it slip that I was interested in placing a small wager on the outcome... you should have heard the words he used!

I can't believe it! You're the first rookie in... Let me think... I can't even remember... It's been at least a month. Well done!
Phew, good thing I didn't bet against. I would've ended up losing my shirt...
It's an honor for every fallen warrior if his body serves as a model for the creation of clones!
Oh! That's just what we needed. Soon we'll create these new bodies, breathe Sparks into them, and our fallen brothers and sisters will rejoin us once again!
Fear weakens us, but feeds the demons. Is that not perfection?!

Oh good, our food's here. Thank you kindly. Where are our boys? Hey! Time to refuel! You'd better go. Hungry demons are nothing to fool with. And you don't have clearance to rub shoulders with such higher beings!
Speak with Nomarkh Ankh to teleport to the Palace Square, enter the pyramid and get the answers you need.

I've only had you do one thing for me this whole time... But you didn't assume that this was all the all-mighty god would ask of you, did you? This agreement with Nihaz has another, greater purpose! And now it is time to reveal this to you.
You've only heard one revelation, the Revelation of Nihaz, which with his usual bloody-minded sense of humor he has nicknamed Tka-Rik's Revelation. Just as there's no yin without yang, no west without the east, there's no Truth without two sides of the truth. You heard the word of darkness, but soon you'll know the word of Light! The real, true Light, the Creating and All-Merciful Light that is Sarn!
Your path lies to the depths of Tep's ancient pyramid! I don't know what awaits you there. The answers to our questions do not always bring joy. I hope that you'll make the right decision.

An obelisk stands before you. Its smooth, black surface swallows up all of even the brightest light. The longer you stare into it, the more you'll change. It already appears as if the obelisk is looking back at you, its gaze piercing to your very soul!
You feel an irresistible urge to touch its surface. Such a smooth, perfect blackness, so alluring...
Touch the black stone and come to understand its purpose.
You are drawn to touch its cold surface. Something drives you to touch it, and you cannot resist the urge...

Greetings, Keeper of the Revelation!
The enemy tried to cloud your mind with false words, and I am happy that you did not give in to his seductive promises!

Unfortunately, as I expected, the alliance with the demons came to nought. the Dead City remains inaccessible...
But don't get depressed! Be happy!
The Master was merciful enough to reveal his thoughts to me. You will get to where you are going. This time, no broken June portals or any of that museum-ready ancient technology.
This time you are going to be witness to the greatest event in the world - an act of Creation! The creation of matter from the astral! We will create our own path to the Dead City!
Meet with Nihaz in the Master's Citadel.

Come on, the Master is waiting! Hearken to his words as we all have; the Master's wisdom is without bounds.
Long ago he came to understand things that you inhabitants of Sarnaut can't even imagine!

I see. You probably came to me for a bit of ancient wisdom? To learn secrets? To come closer to the unknown? Well, well...
Remember what I said? The only worthwhile wisdom is one that you achieve yourself. What do you need other people's ideas for, when you've got your own head on your shoulders? Think about it.
As far as the Seals are concerned... I wonder if you understand that the Seals are manifestations of God's power. Who, if not a God, could wield pure Power? Only another, stronger Power. I defeated Sarn at the dawn of time...well, the "dawn" as you might understand it. To defeat someone means you are more powerful. And I manifested my power into locks that I placed on Sarn. So far you have encountered only one manifestation of my power, that which you mortals call "the darkness," although that's not quite it. Dark, Light, Good, Evil - all of these are subjective notions, my friend. They are only useful to those who can not see beyond the reality that surrounds them. I wouldn't bother with you or anyone like you if I didn't feel you were capable of transcending the banalities that you've had driven into your skull since birth. So think, my friend, think. Thinking is always worth your while. When you've thought of something interesting, then we'll take up this conversation again.

We'll also learn the most important part of a living thing: nature or nurture? I am confident that we can raise draconids whose hearts will be open to Sarn.

Oh, what beautiful, strong eggs! I can already see the precious, scaly little creatures crawling about the camp and cooing the praises of Sarn. Thank you!
Thank you!
But I still haven't figured out... Who will watch over the eggs? Ah yes, we'll give the task to the Skillful Family. They already deal with demons all day... raising draconids shouldn't be difficult for them.

Listen up. I don't feel entirely comfortable when my consciousness passes over into the mystic plane. It's like I can feel something behind me. I can feel movement, or I can feel eyes upon me. I carefully look around, behind every corner, turn over every rock, even poke my head into every basement, and find no one. But I can't shake that feeling that there's someone here besides me!
 One theory is that it might be one of the Destroyers. It might even be a Terminator - the most dangerous one of their tribe. I can't see them, but that awful feeling at the nape of my neck... I can feel their eyes upon me! Ugh! I have a special amulet that I got from the camp: the beater's amulet. With its help, you can summon a demon possessing an excellent sense of smell. Terminators are invisible to the eye, but they must have a smell. Especially because they spend much of their lives in moldy tombs.
Call the demon hound and, if he can find the Terminators, dispose of them!
It's a feeling that someone's watching us... right now... it's gone! How goes it?
That means there really were Terminators. And now they've been destroyed! I salute you! I can continue my observations in peace.
